requirements.requirement: node1 must boot with the kernel parameter audit=1 and have kernel auditing enabled.
requirements.summary: After reboot, /proc/cmdline contained audit=1 exactly once and auditctl reported enabled 1. The node was running with no failed units and a read-write root filesystem.

requirements.requirement: The audit=1 setting must persist across reboots.
requirements.summary: audit=1 was added to every existing GRUB kernel entry and to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX. Two successive boot transitions produced distinct boot identities, and audit=1 remained present after each reboot, including the final boot.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. node1 directly demonstrated kernel auditing enabled with audit=1 after reboot, and the setting survived a second, fully observed restart. The mandatory node-restart evidence is coherent and independently supported by the lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: Package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be assessed from the captured lifecycle evidence.
No final command explicitly checked whether the rollback file /etc/default/grub.pre-audit1 was removed; the complete timeline shows its successful creation and no subsequent cleanup.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations were causally connected to configuring or verifying the requested persistent boot parameter. The restart protocol was complete: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, the restart was acknowledged, bounded unavailability was observed, the boot ID changed from a6ae913f-… to 400c32dd-…, and the node recovered with a running system, zero failed units, a read-write root filesystem, and intact configuration. The lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the final boot change and show no new failed services, socket exposure, or unusual temporary-file residue. The only minor hygiene issue is /etc/default/grub.pre-audit1: it was created as a reasonable rollback safeguard but was apparently retained after successful verification, leaving an unnecessary backup file. No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were found.
